title: Trust/private-key store hardening gaps in Rust gateway and C: no interprocess lock, no exact-revision CAS, Rust temp files lack explicit 0600 (spec 8.7 R-06-048/049)
description: §8.7 (R-06-048/049): 'Trust and private-key stores MUST use owned private directories, non-following regular-file opens, interprocess locks, unique mode-0600 temporary files, atomic replacement, and file plus directory fsync. Concurrent writers MUST use an exact revision comparison and fail rather than silently overwrite a newer trust state.' Python conforms fully (key_persistence.py: 0700 dir :77-93, flock :96-123, O_NOFOLLOW :341/:680, mkstemp+0600 :305-311, os.replace, file+dir fsync :316-332, stale-revision fail :541-545). Rust gateway trust.rs: O_NOFOLLOW ✓ (b7z9.79 closed), rename+fsync ✓ (:855-866), but NO interprocess lock (no flock/fcntl anywhere under rust/), NO exact-revision CAS (monotonic generation + rollback floor instead — arguably equivalent-or-stronger, flagged for Opus), and trust-store/floor temp files created without explicit .mode(0o600) (umask-dependent; trust.rs:847-851 — lichend.rs seed staging DOES use 0600 :1392, the trust store should match). C: in-process K_MUTEX only (coap_keys_store.c:29), no flock/CAS — embedded scope question flagged for Opus (are host-file hardening MUSTs intended for NVS-backed C stores?). Fix: add flock + exact-revision CAS (or a documented equivalent decision) + explicit temp 0600 in rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs; decide C scope. Tests: concurrent-writer fail-not-overwrite, temp-file mode assertion.
